reason: Data persistence section: additional volumes created and attached at launch are not deleted on termination by default; setting DeleteOnTermination to true at launch changes this, and the next sentence says the volumes are then deleted.

Same section: the root volume created at launch is deleted on termination by default; DeleteOnTermination false at launch keeps it, and the context sentence says it can then be attached to another instance.
Considerations on the detach page state verbatim that a root device volume can be detached only after the instance is stopped.

The first clause is supported, but the quote says data on a volume detached during in-progress writes 'might be out of sync', not that in-progress writes can be lost; the claim says more than the quote.

Pricing example 9: ListChangedBlocks and ListSnapshotBlocks are charged per request; GetSnapshotBlock and (in the quoted context) PutSnapshotBlock are charged per SnapshotAPIUnit, one 512 KiB block per request.
The page states pre and post scripts in policies that target instances automate application-consistent snapshots; pre script freezes and flushes I/O before creation, post script thaws I/O.
Important note under the archive retention step: the minimum retention period for archived snapshots is 90 days.
Note in the policy creation steps: archiving can be enabled only for monthly or yearly frequency or a cron expression with a frequency of at least 28 days.
The overview page says DLM automates creation, retention and deletion of EBS snapshots and EBS-backed AMIs, and provides the backup solution at no additional cost.
Important box on the overview page states both restrictions verbatim.

The cross-account page describes copying to specific Regions in an isolated account with encryption to protect against a compromised account; source shares, target event policy copies; both policies in the same Region.
Cross-Region copy step: a schedule creating snapshots in a Region can copy to up to three additional Regions or Outposts, one rule per destination.
Target resource tags section: custom policies use tags; all resources of the targeted type with at least one target tag are targeted.
The Policies section lists the three custom policy types with the same targets and actions as the claim.
Configure schedule step: a policy can have up to 4 schedules; schedule 1 mandatory, 2 to 4 optional.
Default policies back up all volumes and instances in a Region without recent backups; only one default policy per resource type per account and Region.
Considerations for default policies state the random four-hour window and backup at the creation frequency verbatim.
Considerations for default policies: default policies only start targeting resources at least 24 hours old.

Snapshot policy comparison table rows: cross-account sharing No/Yes and application-consistent snapshots No/Yes using pre and post scripts, for default versus custom EBS snapshot policies, matching the qualifier scope.
Resource targeting row of the comparison table states both sides of the claim, including the exclusion parameters.
General considerations for snapshot lifecycle policies state both timing rules verbatim.
Snapshot creation frequency row: default every 1 to 7 days; custom daily, weekly, monthly, yearly or cron.
Snapshot retention row: default 2 to 14 days; custom up to 1000 snapshots count-based or up to 100 years age-based.
Supported retention types row: default age-based only; custom age-based and count-based.
Schedule steps: runs daily, weekly, monthly or yearly, or a custom cron expression (context); retention by total count or age.
Support multiple schedules row: default No; custom Yes, up to 4 schedules per policy.
Elastic Volumes considerations: up to four modifications per volume in a rolling 24-hour period while in-use or available and all previous modifications completed.
Intro of the Elastic Volumes page states the three changes and, when the instance supports Elastic Volumes, no detach or restart.
Note on the initialization page states the claim verbatim; context limits initialization to volumes from snapshots or copies.
Encrypt unencrypted resources section gives the restriction and both workarounds verbatim.
The two encryption-examples sections state the outcome without and with encryption by default exactly as claimed.
Data encryption section quotes the claim verbatim.
Three quotes: all EC2 instance types support EBS encryption, current and previous generation, and encryption by default on all of them.
Data encryption section: all EBS volume types support encryption.
How EBS encryption works: unique AWS managed key per Region, alias aws/ebs, used by default, symmetric customer managed key as an alternative.
Data encryption section states the first-volume key creation and its use unless a customer managed key is used.
Encryption by default page: enforces encryption of new volumes and snapshot copies; no effect on existing volumes or snapshots.
Considerations list states the Region-specific setting and the per-volume restriction verbatim.
EBS encryption page states the claim verbatim.
EBS encryption page: the KMS key of an existing snapshot or volume cannot change; a different key can be set during a snapshot copy.
